chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, from Abān ibn Taghlib, who said:
I prayed behind Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام at al-Muzdalifah, and when I finished, he turned toward me and said: “O Abān,

the five obligatory prayers—whoever upholds their limits and guards their appointed times shall meet Allah on the Day of Resurrection while he has with Him a covenant by which He will admit him into Paradise. And whoever does not uphold their limits and does not guard their appointed times shall meet Allah with no covenant for him; if He wills, He will punish him, and if He wills, He will forgive him.”

key_terms.الصَّلَوَاتُ الْخَمْسُ الْمَفْرُوضَاتُ: the five divinely mandated daily prayers
key_terms.الْجَنَّةَ: Paradise, the abode of divine reward
key_terms.حُدُودَهُنَّ: their prescribed limits, conditions, and requirements
key_terms.عَهْدٌ: a covenant or assured promise with Allah
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ: the Day of Resurrection and final judgment

ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of observing or neglecting the five obligatory prayers in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith emphasizes the central importance of the five obligatory salat (prayers), especially observing their proper limits and appointed times. It presents faithful performance of salat as a cause of divine covenant and entry into Paradise, while neglect of it leaves a person exposed to Allah’s judgment, whether punishment or forgiveness.
